docs.title: Libraries
docs.text:
ALL my main libraries have been updated to support following KMP targets (if possible):

  • jvm
  • android
  • ios
  • macos
  • wasm

docs.title: Experimental
docs.text:
Why do some libraries use experimental functions?

Mostly I do use androidx.compose.ui.backhandler.BackHandler and the the kotlinx.datetime.Clock class. Both are currently still marked as experimental. I need both to support all the platforms so I do use those...

docs.title: Unofficial Libraries
docs.text: Unofficial Libraries Library Minimum Version Latest Version Info kmp-parcelize ALL used internally in my libraries - it offers kmp compatible parcelize annotations that do map to the android parcelize ones on android and to "empty implementations" on other platforms kmp-library ALL just a utility for the gradle setups kmp-democomposables - just used for library demos, they are not meant for any other public use Toolbox - this is for my personal use - it offers A LOT like a whole base app for a kmp project that renders on all platforms differently, a table class, many reusable UI elements and more...

docs.title: Binary Compatibility
docs.text:
I do try to keep versions binary compatible as long as possible now. If a non binary compatible change is unavoidable the major version will be increased.

Note

All minor versions are binary compatible.
